names: United Kingdoms of Sweden and Norway
title: United Kingdoms of Sweden and Norway
capsule: The union between Sweden and Norway was a personal union constituted by the Convention of Moss (14 August 1814) and confirmed by the Norwegian Storting's election of the Swedish king Karl XIII on 4 November 1814, following Napoleon's defeat and the Treaty of Kiel by which Denmark ceded Norway to Sweden. The two kingdoms retained entirely separate constitutions, laws, and parliaments, sharing only the monarch and a joint foreign-affairs ministry — a constitutional arrangement that made it one of the most liberal unions of its era. Mounting Norwegian demands for a separate consular service and full diplomatic independence produced a constitutional crisis; Norway's Storting unilaterally dissolved the union on 7 June 1905, and the Karlstad Convention (26 October 1905) settled the separation peacefully, with Norwegian prince Carl of Denmark crowned as King Haakon VII.
